messages.text:
"PROJETO: REAL FLIGHT SIMULATOR 3D — MOBILE

Desenvolva um simulador de aviação 3D com realismo extremo, inspirado na aviação real. Utilize Unity/Unreal como referência de arquitetura, C# para sistemas quando disponível, Blender para modelagem, shaders PBR, iluminação dinâmica, física baseada em forças e renderização otimizada para mobile.

1. AERONAVES: Crie aviões comerciais, pequenos monomotores e jatos executivos, com modelagem 3D detalhada. Fuselagem, asas, turbinas, hélices, flaps, leme, profundores, spoilers, rodas e trem de pouso devem ter geometria, materiais e animações individuais. Cockpit completo com instrumentos funcionais, telas, botões e iluminação interna.

2. FÍSICA DE VOO: Desenvolva um sistema aerodinâmico próprio baseado em sustentação, gravidade, arrasto, empuxo, massa, inércia, densidade do ar e ângulo de ataque. Simule rolagem, arfagem, guinada, turbulência, vento lateral, estol e perda de sustentação. Flaps, profundores, leme e ailerons devem alterar fisicamente o comportamento da aeronave. Cada modelo deve possuir características próprias de peso, potência e aerodinâmica.

3. MOTORES E SISTEMAS: Criar motores com aceleração progressiva, resposta de potência, consumo de combustível, temperatura e funcionamento independente. Implementar freios, reversores quando aplicáveis, trem de pouso retrátil, amortecimento das rodas e sistemas de controle funcionais.

4. CENÁRIOS: Construir um mundo 3D extenso com cidades, bairros, edifícios, estradas, florestas, montanhas, rios, oceanos e aeroportos. Utilizar terreno procedural, chunks, LOD e texturas PBR. Criar pistas com sinalização, iluminação, terminais, hangares, torres de controle, veículos de serviço e objetos ambientais detalhados.

5. ATMOSFERA: Implementar nuvens volumétricas em diferentes altitudes, neblina, iluminação solar, sombras dinâmicas, reflexos, ciclo de dia e noite, amanhecer e pôr do sol. Criar clima dinâmico com chuva, tempestades, ventos e turbulências que realmente influenciem o voo.

6. POPULAÇÃO E AMBIENTE: Adicionar pessoas em aeroportos, passageiros, funcionários, equipes de solo e veículos de serviço. Utilizar personagens 3D com animações naturais, movimentação independente e comportamentos ambientais. Criar aeroportos vivos, sem personagens estáticos repetidos.

7. INTERAÇÃO E CONTROLES: Criar controles mobile com joystick virtual, inclinação, manche, acelerador, freios, flaps e trem de pouso. Implementar câmeras de cockpit, externa, lateral e perseguição. Permitir interação com instrumentos e comandos da cabine. Interface profissional com velocidade, altitude, direção, combustível e informações de voo.

8. ÁUDIO: Implementar áudio espacial para motores, turbinas, hélices, vento, chuva, cabine, alarmes e ambiente aeroportuário. Os sons devem variar conforme velocidade, potência, distância e posição da câmera.

9. OTIMIZAÇÃO: Utilizar LOD, occlusion culling, iluminação otimizada, carregamento progressivo, instancing e redução de objetos distantes. Criar configurações gráficas reais: Baixo, Médio, Alto e Ultra, alterando resolução, sombras, vegetação, partículas e distância de renderização. Buscar 30–60 FPS estáveis conforme o dispositivo.

10. REGRA DE DESENVOLVIMENTO: Não criar sistemas apenas visuais ou botões sem função. Cada componente precisa estar conectado à física, aos controles e ao restante do jogo. Priorizar realismo visual, coerência física, animações naturais, profundidade ambiental e desempenho mobile. Construir um simulador completo, integrado e jogável, não apenas uma demonstração visual.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

The user wants a complete 3D flight simulator game. This is a big build request. They mention Unity/Unreal as reference architecture, C#, Blender, etc. — but I'm working in a web environment where I can build HTML/JS/Three.js games. The pragmatic approach: build a web-based 3D flight simulator using Three.js (JavaScript), which runs in a browser and can be tested with screenshots. The instructions say "Build a complete, playable game now" and don't ask clarifying questions.

Let me check the working directory first to see what exists.

Let me plan the game:

**Real Flight Simulator 3D — Mobile** in Three.js:

1. Aircraft: at least 2-3 aircraft types (commercial airliner, small single-prop, executive jet) built procedurally with Three.js geometry — fuselage, wings, engines/propellers, control surfaces (flaps, ailerons, rudder, elevators), landing gear. Animated control surfaces and gear.

2. Flight physics: custom aerodynamics — lift, drag, thrust, gravity, angle of attack, stall, air density varying with altitude, control surfaces affecting pitch/roll/yaw, flaps changing lift/drag, turbulence and wind.

3. Engines: progressive throttle spool-up, fuel consumption, temperature, brakes, reverse thrust, retractable gear.

4. Scenery: procedural terrain with chunks/LOD, city buildings (instanced), roads, forests, mountains, ocean, airport with runway markings, terminal, hangar, control tower.

5. Atmosphere: day/night cycle, sun, fog, clouds (billboard/volumetric-ish), weather (rain particles, wind).

6. Population: people at airport (simple animated NPCs walking), service vehicles moving.

7. Controls: mobile virtual joystick + throttle, flaps, gear, brakes, cameras (cockpit, external, chase, side), HUD with speed, altitude, heading, fuel.

8. Audio: WebAudio synthesized engine sounds varying with RPM, wind, alarms (stall).

9. Optimization: LOD, instancing, graphics settings (Low/Medium/High/Ultra), fog distance, shadows.

10. Everything connected — no dead buttons.

That's a lot, but doable in a single-page Three.js app. I should write it in modular JS files (or one big file). Let me structure:

- `index.html`
- `src/main.js` — bootstrap
- `src/physics.js` — flight model
- `src/aircraft.js` — aircraft builders
- `src/world.js` — terrain, airport, city
- `src/weather.js`
- `src/audio.js`
- `src/controls.js`
- `src/hud.js`
- `src/npc.js`

Actually, for simplicity and to avoid module loading issues, maybe use ES modules with importmap from CDN (three.js). The environment may be offline? Let me check if there's network access. I can test with a local server and puppeteer? Do I have puppeteer available? Let me check the workspace.

Let me look at the working directory first.

I'll check what's in /home/runner/work/Rfs/Rfs. Then decide. There may be an existing game (the prompt says "or apply the requested change to the existing game"). Let me explore.

For screenshots: I need a headless browser. Check if puppeteer/playwright is installed, or if chromium is available. If no network, I need three.js locally — maybe write my own minimal 3D? That would be huge. Better to check for node_modules with three, or npm availability.

Let me start exploring.

Plan:
1. Explore workspace, check tools (node, npm, chromium/puppeteer).
2. Set up project with three.js (via npm or vendored).
3. Write the simulator code in modules.
4. Test with headless browser screenshots, iterate.
5. Final response with assumptions.

Let me begin.


Use importmap pointing at ./vendor/three.module.js. Vendor it via npm/curl.

Key systems to implement (all must be functional per rule 10):

**Physics (physics.js)** — the core. Rigid-body-ish 6DOF model:
- State: position (Vector3), velocity (Vector3 world), orientation (quaternion), angular velocity (body rates p,q,r).
- Forces: 
  - Thrust along body forward axis, scaled by throttle with spool lag, and by air density.
  - Lift perpendicular to airflow in body-up direction: L = 0.5 * rho * V^2 * S * CL(alpha). CL is a curve: linear up to stall alpha (~15-16°, less with flaps), then drops (stall). CL0 + CLalpha*alpha + flap contribution.
  - Drag: D = 0.5*rho*V^2*S*(CD0 + k*CL^2 + flap/gear/spoiler extras + reverse drag).
  - Side force from sideslip (beta).
  - Gravity.
- Moments: control surfaces produce angular accelerations scaled by dynamic pressure (q), plus aerodynamic damping, plus static stability (weathervane yaw toward velocity, pitch stability), plus roll from aileron, yaw from rudder. Also stall behavior: loss of control effectiveness when stalled.
- Air density: rho = rho0 * exp(-alt/H).
- Wind: vector field, wind + turbulence (Perlin-ish noise), crosswind affects velocity used in aero calcs.
- Ground handling: when gear touching ground, wheels support normal force, friction/brakes, steering with rudder at low speed; crash detection when hitting ground too fast / wrong attitude (gear up, excessive vertical speed, off-runway rough terrain slows/destroys).

Simplify but keep it "force-based": compute alpha = angle between velocity and body forward projected onto pitch plane, beta for sideslip. Angular dynamics: angular acceleration = (moment / I) - damping. This is achievable and feels good.

**Aircraft (aircraft.js)** — three craft with distinct params:
1. "Cessna" style single-prop: low mass (1100 kg), prop thrust curve, high drag, forgiving stall, fixed gear option... but spec says retractable gear — give it retractable too (many have fixed, but fine, make it retractable).
2. Executive jet ("Executive Jet"): mid mass, twin engines, swept wings.
3. Commercial airliner ("Airliner"): heavy, twin turbofans, flaps 3 stages, spoilers, reverse thrust.

Each built procedurally from Three geometry with named parts: propeller/turbine fan spin, flaps that rotate, ailerons, elevators, rudder, gear that retracts (animate), spinning wheels. Cockpit interior: instrument panel visible in cockpit view — with live gauges (canvas textures for PFD-ish screens? maybe simple 3D needles). Keep cockpit simple but functional: panel with airspeed/attitude/altimeter gauges drawn on canvas textures updated at low rate.

**World (world.js)**:
- Procedural terrain: large plane with heightfield from noise; chunks around plane with LOD (2-3 rings). Simple approach: a grid of chunks (e.g., 7x7) each 800m, geometry detail by distance, height from fBm noise; vertex colors for terrain (grass, rock, sand, snow). Ocean plane at y=0 with animated shader-ish (just semi-transparent blue with specular + moving normals via time uniform? keep simple: MeshPhongMaterial with env reflection, slight vertex wave animation on a low-res grid).
- Airport at a flat spot: runway 2500m with markings (canvas texture), taxiway, terminal building, hangar, control tower, runway edge lights (instanced), approach lights.
- City: instanced boxes with PBR-ish materials (metalness/roughness + emissive windows at night), roads as dark strips, forest: instanced cone+cylinder trees on terrain where height suitable, mountains from noise.
- Runway lights emissive at night.

**Weather (weather.js)**:
- Day/night cycle: sun position, sky color lerp, fog color, hemisphere light, stars at night, sun/moon sprite.
- Clouds: billboard sprites (canvas-generated soft blobs) at 2 altitude layers, drift with wind.
- Rain: particle system (Points) around camera when storm; lightning flash light occasionally; storm increases wind/turbulence.
- Settings: clear / cloudy / storm; wind slider effect.

**NPC (npc.js)**:
- People at airport: capsule+sphere low-poly humanoids, instanced or individual meshes (~20), walking along paths on the apron with leg swing animation, random behaviors (walk to gate, stand). Service vehicles: baggage cart and fuel truck driving loops on taxiway with wheel rotation.
- They must not be static/repeated: vary colors, speeds, routes.

**Controls (controls.js)**:
- Virtual joystick (left, pitch/roll), throttle slider (right side), buttons: gear, flaps step, brakes (hold), spoilers, reverse, camera cycle, pause. Keyboard support for desktop (arrows/WASD, PageUp/Down throttle, G/B/F/C). Tilt option? "inclinação" — add device orientation toggle using DeviceOrientationEvent (mobile). Implement but guard.
- Touch handling multi-touch proper.

**HUD (hud.js)**:
- Speed, altitude (barometric from rho), heading, VS, throttle %, fuel, flaps/gear/brakes indicators, stall warning, AGL, ILS-ish guidance to runway? Maybe simple "AP" — skip autopilot, or simple heading hold? Keep: HUD + mini gauges + warning lights. Also minimap? Skip minimap; add compass strip.

**Audio (audio.js)**:
- WebAudio: engine = oscillators+noise filtered, pitch/volume from RPM & throttle; jet = filtered noise; wind noise from airspeed; stall alarm beeper; gear horn; touch down squeak? Keep: engine, jet, wind, alarm, click sounds. Spatial: stereo pan based on camera relative to aircraft (simple StereoPanner).

**Settings/Optimization (settings.js)**:
- Low/Medium/High/Ultra: render scale (setPixelRatio), shadows on/off + map size, cloud count, tree/city draw distance (fog & far plane), tree count, rain particles count. Auto FPS adjust? Maybe optional; keep manual 4 presets.

**Main loop**: fixed timestep physics (e.g., 120 Hz substeps), render.

Crash/restart: reset button when crashed, with overlay message.

Fuel: consumption from throttle, empty -> engines cut. Engine temperature rises with throttle, overheat warning.

Given the scale, I'll write the code in several files but keep each focused. Total maybe ~3500 lines. Let's be efficient and write carefully to minimize iteration cycles. I need to be careful with three.js r160 API: 
- `outputColorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace`
- `THREE.sRGBEncoding` removed.
- Lights: use `renderer.useLegacyLights = false` (default in newer), intensities in physical units — with r160, useLegacyLights default false? In r155+, default is false (physically correct). So directional light intensity ~2-3, hemisphere ~0.5-1.
- InstancedMesh for trees/buildings/people? People need animation — use individual low-poly meshes (20 is fine) with skinned-like transform animation via limb rotation.
- Sprite for clouds with canvas texture.

Terrain chunks: implement ChunkedTerrain class: chunk size 600, radius 5 chunks (~3.6km view) with LOD by distance: near chunks 32x32 segments, far 12x12, farthest 6x6. Rebuild when plane crosses chunk boundary. Use vertex colors. Add getGroundHeight(x,z) function shared for collision — same noise function used to displace vertices. Runway area flattened: blend height to a flat plateau near airport.

Ocean: big plane at y = 0 where terrain below 0? Make terrain heights range from -30 to 900. Where ground height < water level (y=2?), draw water plane covering whole world at y=0 (large plane following camera x/z). Terrain below 0 shows water. Simple and works.

Mountains: noise with ridged component far from airport. City: place on flat-ish land near airport.

Let me define the noise: implement simple value noise with hash, fBm 4-5 octaves. Deterministic seeded.

Airport: runway along X axis from -1250 to +1250 at z=0, width 45m. Flatten terrain within rectangle |x|<1500, |z|<250 to y=8 (plateau height). Hmm, terrain height function must return exactly 8 inside the flattened region with smooth blend margin 200m. Plateau height 8m above sea so ocean doesn't flood.

City: cluster of blocks at z between 300 and 1500, x -1500..1500, on plateau-ish area; ensure ground there is flatten-blended too or accept slope — extend flatten region with hills beyond. Fine.

Trees: instanced (trunk InstancedMesh + crown InstancedMesh), placed where height between 4 and 250 and outside airport rect, within 3km, ~600 trees (Ultra), fewer at low settings. Also forest clusters.

Buildings: instanced boxes with varying scale, color via instanceColor; emissive windows via texture on box? InstancedMesh can't vary emissive easily; use one window texture (canvas) with emissiveMap, emissiveIntensity animated at night. That gives night city glow. 

Roads: dark planes strips on ground within city grid + highway from city to airport.

People: 16 individuals: body (capsule via cylinder+spheres), head sphere, legs (2 boxes animated swing), arms. Walking along apron near terminal; some stand. Colors varied. Service vehicles: fuel truck follows loop around apron; baggage tug with carts follows straight path.

Controls detail:
- Left joystick: pitch (up/down) & roll (left/right). Also rudder via two small buttons? Add L/R rudder buttons near throttle.
- Right vertical slider: throttle 0..1. Buttons column: GEAR, FLAPS+, BRK (hold), RVS toggle (only on ground), SPR (spoilers), CAM, and settings gear.
- Top bar: HUD readouts. Warnings center: STALL / OVERSPEED / GEAR / FUEL.
- Pause menu: settings modal with graphics preset, weather, time of day slider, tilt toggle, sound toggle, aircraft select + spawn (airport or airborne 500m).

Aircraft select in start overlay: choose aircraft + start condition (runway / air). Start overlay is needed anyway for audio unlock (user gesture) — good: "START" button unlocks AudioContext.

Cockpit view: camera at pilot position; show cockpit group (panel, yoke visible? panel with gauges as canvas textures: airspeed needle, attitude indicator, altimeter, plus throttle levers animating). Update canvas textures at 10Hz. Interior light at night (point light small). This satisfies "cockpit with functional instruments".

Cameras: 0 cockpit, 1 external orbit (drag to orbit), 2 chase (follow behind smoothed), 3 side/flyby (fixed offset). Wheel/pinch zoom for external.

Screenshots: I'll take a few during dev; keep viewport 1280 wide (playwright-cli resize 1280x720), save as .jpg via screenshot command? The CLI screenshot has --filename; format png by default. It said save small JPEGs with .jpg path — screenshot may support format by extension; if not, convert with ImageMagick? Check `convert` availability. Or capture via eval canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg')? Simpler: take PNG then convert with node canvas? Easiest: use `screenshot --filename=x.jpg` and see output format; else convert via ffmpeg/convert. Let me check available converters later. Actually I can read PNG directly only when fine detail matters — reading a 1280x720 PNG is fine-ish but instruction says prefer jpg ≤1280 wide. I'll convert with `convert` (ImageMagick) if present, else ffmpeg, else read PNG.

Physics tuning: I must be careful the planes fly. Approach: normalized aero with real-ish numbers:
- Cessna: m=1100kg, S=16.2, CL0=0.3, CLa=5.0/rad, stall alpha 16°, CD0=0.03, k=0.045, max thrust ~3200N static (prop with drop-off with speed: T = T0*(1 - 0.35*V/Vmax-ish)).
- Jet: m=8000kg, S=26, twin engines 2x14kN, CD0=0.022.
- Airliner: m=60000kg, S=180, 2x110kN, CD0=0.024, flaps big effect.

Check level flight: airliner at 250 kt (~128 m/s) at sea level rho=1.225: q=0.5*1.225*128^2 ≈ 10035; L=q*S*CL => CL = 60000*9.81/(10035*180) ≈ 0.326. OK. Cruise thrust = D: CD = 0.024+0.045*0.106=0.0288; D=10035*180*0.0288 ≈ 52kN < 220kN. Fine, accelerates then drag rises. Good.

OH NO. I see the bug!!! The quaternion integration multiplies dq ON THE RIGHT:

```js
const dq = new THREE.Quaternion(w.x*halfDt, w.y*halfDt, w.z*halfDt, 0);
dq.multiply(this.quat);
this.quat.x += dq.x; ...
```

The standard small-angle body-rate integration: q' = q + 0.5 * q ⊗ ω_body. That means dq_quat = 0.5*dt*(q ⊗ ω). My code: dq = ω_quat * q (ω on the LEFT = world frame!) — multiplication ORDER: dq.multiply(this.quat) computes dq = dq * q where dq=(wx,wy,wz,0)... So q' = q + (ω ⊗ q) — that's ω in the WORLD frame, but my rates are BODY rates! The multiplication should be q ⊗ ω: 

```js
const dq = this.quat.clone().multiply(new THREE.Quaternion(w.x*halfDt, w.y*halfDt, w.z*halfDt, 0));
```

With the wrong order, the pitch rate (body X) is applied about the WORLD X axis instead of body X! At spawn heading 90° (nose +X world): body pitch axis (right wing) points along world -Z... applying rotation about world X = ROLLING the aircraft (about its nose axis)! That's why euler.x didn't change — the pitch was applied as something else — and the ground clamp then zeroed the roll, canceling everything!!!

```js
const dq = new THREE.Quaternion(w.x * halfDt, w.y * halfDt, w.z * halfDt, 0);
```

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile 3D flight simulator ("REAL FLIGHT SIMULATOR 3D — MOBILE") per the user's 10-point Portuguese spec: 3 aircraft with animated control surfaces, force-based flight physics, engines/fuel/temperature, procedural world with airport/city/trees, weather/day-night cycle, animated NPC population, mobile touch controls, synthesized audio, and 4 graphics quality presets — everything functional and integrated, no dead buttons.

## Requirements
- Build now as a complete playable game; no clarifying questions; note assumptions briefly when finished.
- Verify visually via screenshots saved as small JPEGs (viewport ≤1280px wide); read only the latest screenshot.
- Every component must connect to physics/controls (user's rule 10).

## Decisions
- Built as browser-based Three.js app (r160, vendored at `vendor/three.module.js`) instead of Unity/Unreal, since environment is web/screenshot-based; mobile-first UI.
- Aircraft: cessna (prop), jet (executive), airliner — procedural models with animated flaps/ailerons/elevator/rudder/gear/prop/fans/lights, plus canvas-gauge cockpit (`CockpitInstruments`).
- Physics: custom 6DOF force model in `src/physics.js` (lift/drag/CL-vs-alpha stall/sideslip/density/wind/turbulence), body-frame angular rates, quaternion integration, hybrid ground model with euler-clamp attitude.
- Conventions: nose = +Z body axis, +euler.x = nose DOWN; debug API exposed as `window.SIM` (state, step, setInput, tp, raycast, sceneObj, envObj, inputObj, game, camObj); `window.__errors` captures JS errors (capped at 20).
- Test loop: `python3 -m http.server 3002` serving repo root; playwright-cli (resize 1280x720) for screenshots/evals; physics validated numerically via `SIM.step()` before visual checks.

## Work State
### Completed
- All source files written: `index.html`, `src/main.js`, `src/physics.js`, `src/aircraft.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/env.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/controls.js`, `src/hud.js`; three.js vendored.

Why does IAS decay so fast? At full nose-up trim alpha ~14-15°, CL ≈ 0.33+5.05*0.25 = 1.6, CD = 0.034 + 0.055*2.56 + gear 0.02 = 0.195! Drag = qbar*S*CD. At 63kt=32.4 m/s: qbar 643, drag = 643*16.2*0.195 = 2032 N. Thrust ~3800 N. Should still accelerate...

Wait but the CLIMB angle: VS 3385 fpm = 17 m/s at 32 m/s → γ = 32°! sin(32°) = 0.53 → gravity component along path = 9810*0.53 = 5200 N >> thrust 3800 - drag 2000 = 1800. So decelerating hard. The plane pulled into a steep climb because at rotation speed with full elevator the vertical energy conversion is huge.

Real Cessna: Vy climb at 74-85 kt, climb angle ~7°. The issue: elevator at full deflection during climb-out trims alpha 14-15°, and the resulting flight path with thrust is steep, bleeding energy.

The "correct" sim behavior: at full aft stick you'd get this kind of decelerating zoom climb — that's pilot error, honestly! Full elevator held through climb-out IS excessive. A real pilot backs off. My test protocol holds 0.62 for 8s — an unrealistic input.

But for game feel, the plane should be forgiving: holding full up shouldn't depart into a fatal stall crash within 8 seconds. Two mitigations:
1. Cap the elevator trim alpha lower (steeper blanking): make full-stick trim ~12° (below stall 16.2°) → CL ~1.28, less drag, gentler climb. 
2. Add pitch-rate limiting: with damping, ω.x equilibrium = -0.25 rad/s is high; reduce pitchPow a bit or increase pitchDamp for smoother feel.

Also the phugoid: speed 63→17 while VS positive means it converted ALL kinetic energy to altitude. A Cessna at 63kt with full aft stick WOULD decelerate to stall — but a real one at full aft stick also has the wing at CLmax ~1.6-2.0 (flaps) and the departure is softer. Our test: hold 0.62 pitch for 8 full seconds post-rotation — that's just wrong piloting. Let me test realistic rotation: pitch up until airborne, then ease to climb attitude (pitch input ~0.3), keep ~60-65kt, VS ~800-1200 fpm.

But ALSO tune blanking to trim lower alpha: change blank start from aStall*0.7 to aStall*0.55 and floor from 0.1 to 0.06: equilibrium full stick: 0.62*15*blank = 9*(alpha-2°)*... alpha=12° (0.209): blank = 1-(0.209-0.156)/0.154 = 0.65 → LHS 6.05... wait: 0.62*15=9.3; 9.3*0.65 = 6.05 vs RHS 9*(0.209-0.035) = 1.57. Hmm LHS >> RHS — alpha keeps rising. My earlier equilibrium calc: full-stick trim at alpha where 9.3*blank(alpha) = 9*(alpha-0.035):
- alpha 18° (0.314): blank = 1-(0.314-0.156)/0.154 = -0.026 → 0.06 floor → LHS 0.56, RHS 2.5 → falling.
- alpha 15° (0.262): blank = 1-(0.262-0.156)/0.154 = 0.31 → LHS 2.9, RHS 2.05 → rising.
- alpha 16° (0.279): blank = 1-0.123/0.154 = 0.2 → LHS 1.87, RHS 2.2 → falling.
- Trim ≈ 15.5°, just above stall. Hmm.

The real problem isn't trim alpha — it's that trim at alpha 15.5 at LOW SPEED produces a steep climbing flight path with insufficient thrust. Physically correct! The plane is just underpowered for sustained 30° climbs — as it should be. The departure at 21kt is what a real 172 does if you yank full aft at rotation and hold it: hedge-hop, stall, drop a wing.

So for gameplay: make the stall/departure less catastrophic and more recoverable, and make the natural climb-out with sensible input work well. Also increase prop thrust margin so speed retention in climb is better: maxThrust 4300 → 5200? At 63kt drag 2032 + climb need... Level flight at 63kt needs 2032 N. Climb at 1000 fpm (5.1 m/s): power needed = 9810*5.1 = 50 kW ≈ 67 hp extra... thrust equivalent at 32 m/s = 1530 N. Total 3560 N < 4300 ✓. So with PROPER input (back off to ~0.35 stick after liftoff), it should climb at 800-1200 fpm at 60-65kt. 

Test protocol fix: rotate with 0.5, once airborne hold 0.3. Also I'll keep blanking but slightly reduce pitchPow 15→13 and strengthen pitchDamp 16→18 for smoother response, and soften stall departure: raise stallEff floor 0.25 (fine), and the stall CL drop (line 144) `clMax*(1-over/9)` floor 0.35 — at alpha 70° (over 54): CL = max(1.66*(1-6), 0.35) = 0.35 ✓ deep stall keeps some lift. OK.

Additionally: consider reducing the pitch-up moment from thrust line... skip.

Also — IMPORTANT: with the crash at 24.5s the state froze (vs -6643, agl 2, crashed presumably). The crash detection worked (badAtt pitchE > 17 at contact? pitch 16.6 at contact... hmm, actually agl 2 = on gear... crashed → main loop probably freezes the sim and shows the crash UI. Need to verify the restart flow later.

Let me retune: pitchPow 15→13, pitchDamp 16→18, blank start 0.7→0.6*aStall, floor 0.1→0.08. Then test with a realistic input schedule: full 0.6 until airborne (max 5s), then 0.3, monitor 30s. Expect: liftoff ~55kt, climb 700-1300 fpm, IAS 55-70, alpha 6-10°, no stall.

Good progress — blanking capped alpha initially, but holding full aft stick for 8s converts all speed to altitude (63→17 kt) then departs — physically plausible but unforgiving. I'll soften the response (less pitch power, more damping, earlier blanking) and use a realistic rotation→climb input schedule:

Still decaying: at pitch 0.3, alpha drifts 8.4→10.2→13.9, speed 61→26, then departure. The 0.3 stick equilibrium trim is too high. Solve: 0.3*13 = 3.9 = 9*(alpha-0.035)*blank(alpha):
- alpha 10° (0.175): blank = 1-(0.175-0.17)/0.14 = 0.96 → LHS 3.9*0.96 = 3.76 vs RHS 9*0.14 = 1.26 → rising (LHS>RHS).
- alpha 15° (0.262): blank = 1-(0.262-0.17)/0.14 = 0.34 → LHS 1.34 vs RHS 2.05 → falling.
- alpha 12° (0.209): blank = 1-(0.209-0.17)/0.14 = 0.72 → LHS 2.81 vs RHS 1.56 → rising.
- alpha 14° (0.244): blank = 1-0.074/0.14 = 0.47 → LHS 1.84 vs RHS 1.88 ≈ TRIM at 14°.

But CL at 14° = 0.33+5.05*0.244 = 1.56! That's CLmax territory — the plane MUST slow down flying at CLmax with only ~2000 N excess thrust minus climb power... it decelerates until stall. Also pitchStab 9 is too weak in general — real equilibrium for a stable plane at moderate stick should be alpha ~5-8°.

Better approach: strengthen pitchStab substantially (9 → 20). Then:
- 0.3 stick: 3.9*blank = 20*(alpha-0.035): alpha 8° (0.14): blank 1 → LHS 3.9 vs RHS 2.1 → rising; alpha 10°: LHS 3.76 vs RHS 2.8 → rising; alpha 12°: 2.81 vs 3.48 → falling. Trim ≈ 11°. Hmm still highish.
- pitchStab 30: 0.3 stick: alpha 8°: 3.9 vs 3.1 rising; alpha 10°: 3.76 vs 4.05 falling → trim ~9.5°. 
- 0.6 full stick: 7.8*blank = 30*(alpha-0.035): alpha 12°: 7.8*0.72=5.6 vs 5.2 rising; alpha 14°: 7.8*0.47=3.7 vs 6.2 falling → trim ~12.5°. Good — full stick trims just below stall.
- Cruise 0.1 stick: 1.3 = 30*(alpha-0.035)*blank → alpha 5° (0.087): 1.3 vs 1.57 falling; alpha 4°: 1.3 vs 1.16 rising → trim ~4.5°. 

pitchStab 30 also affects gust response: damping ratio... pitchDamp 18 with stab 30: natural freq sqrt(30*qfac)... qfac 0.5: ωn = sqrt(30*0.5)=3.9 rad/s, damping ratio = 18*0.5/(2*3.9) = 1.15 — overdamped, stable, no PIO. 

Also qfac at low speed (rotation): qbar 490/1390 = 0.35: stab effect = 30*0.35 = 10.5 per rad. Fine.

But wait — pitchStab ALSO acts on ground? No — only in air branch. Good.

Also consider: trim 9.5° at 0.3 stick at 60kt gives CL 1.15, lift at 60kt (30.9 m/s): qbar 585, lift = 585*16.2*1.15 = 10900 N > 9810 → climbs gently, speed holds ~60-65. 

One more thing: the stall departure went to alpha 62° — even deep-stalled, elevator blanking (floor 0.08) means recovery depends on pitchStab 30: at alpha 40° (0.7 rad): stab = 30*(0.7-0.035)*qfac*stallEff — stallEff floor 0.25... qfac at low speed ~0.15: 30*0.665*0.15*0.25 = 0.75 rad/s² down. Elevator forward needed... recovery works with forward stick.

Also, pitchStab applies qfac*stallEff — at stall, stab also reduced by stallEff 0.25. Hmm — the tail is stalled too, fine.

I saw cessna 15, jet likely ~8, airliner ~5. Scale stab similarly (×3.3). Actually let me look at the jet/airliner specs to scale sensibly.

The user re-sent the spec. I'm mid-debug on the cockpit view. The flags ARE set and hidden (vis:false for the 3 cockpitHide meshes) — but the raycast still hit a cone at 1.7m... Wait, the raycast was taken in the SAME eval right after setting camMode and raf — before cockpitVisibility ran? Raycaster intersects invisible objects? THREE.Raycaster DOES intersect invisible objects by default unless layers/visible checks... Actually Raycaster.intersectObjects respects `visible === false`? Hmm — no, Raycaster checks object.visible? Let me recall: Mesh.raycast doesn't check visible, and intersectObjects traverses... `intersectObject` in r160: it checks `object.layers` and calls object.raycast; it does NOT skip invisible objects! So the raycast result is misleading. Fine.

But the SCREENSHOT still showed the nose cone visible (black shape). Hmm — or was that black shape the SPINNER (metal cone at z 4.35, radius 0.22 + blades 1.9 long)? The prop blades are 1.9m long boxes — from the cockpit they'd appear as a large dark X in front — at 48kt spinning, a screenshot catches them mid-rotation → a vertical dark bar ✓ That matches the dark vertical bar at center-bottom!

And the black top band: could be... the TAIL? No. Let me think — the screenshot: black top half. What geometry is above the camera and ahead? The WING (y 0.95, z 0..1.55, x ±5.5). Camera at (0, 0.62, 1.1) looking +z with -0.13 pitch. The wing top surface faces UP; from below we see its BOTTOM face — white ✓ (that's the white band at middle). Above the wing in the view = sky. But it's black...

Unless — the wing's FAR EDGE (leading edge z 1.55) is very close above the camera eye line: the angular size: wing bottom at y 0.87, camera y 0.62 → 0.25 above; leading edge z 1.55 is 0.45 ahead → angle atan(0.25/0.45) = 29° ABOVE center. Wing trailing z edge... The wing fills 29°..(backward, behind camera). So the wing appears as a band from 29° up to zenith-ish? Behind the camera the wing extends to z=0 (behind camera at z 1.1? No: z 0 is BEHIND (nose is +z). Camera z 1.1 — wing z range 0..1.55: parts from z<1.1 are behind the camera, z 1.1..1.55 ahead. So ahead-only sliver of wing. Looking UP-forward: the wing bottom is visible in a narrow band above ~29°... 

The BLACK top = maybe the SKY DOME has a bug (black above certain elevation) — recall "env sky" gradient... In earlier chase-cam screenshots the sky was fine (blue gradient + mountains at horizon). Top of that screenshot (11-cruise-chase) — the sky at top was... blue-ish/dark blue? It looked normal.

Hmm wait — in cockpit screenshot 12, the black region occupies from ~25° above center to the very top, and the sky sliver ABOVE that is light blue — that's WEIRD: blue ABOVE black. That looks like a dark OBJECT in front of the sky with gaps at the very top. The object: THE CABIN ROOF?? HIDDEN. The WING seen edge-on? The wing is white...

Look at raycast(0, 0.25) from earlier (BEFORE fixes): hits BoxGeometry at 0.2m (shade) then CircleGeometry 3.3 (gauge). That was the old panel layout. Current layout: gauge at z 1.52, y 0.6 — center of view should hit a GAUGE at ~0.45m. Let me raycast now with up/center/down to identify the black band's geometry (ignoring visible flags): pass ny=+0.5 to look up.

Actually, faster: the shade! I placed shade at panelY+0.52 = 0.82, z 1.6, size (panelW+0.2, 0.44, 0.34) rotated -0.9 rad. Camera (0.62, z 1.1) — the shade is 0.5 ahead, 0.2 above, tilted — it hangs over the view upper-middle!! The shade is in the cockpit group (visible) — dark box — covering the UPPER view ahead = the black band ABOVE the gauges! And the gauges are UNDER it at 0.6... So the view: dash+gauge at center-low, shade black band above the gauges, and sky visible above the shade. The wing white band = below the shade? Hmm, the white band appeared at mid-height BELOW the black band, above the gray dash bottom. So layout top→bottom: sky sliver, BLACK (shade), white band (wing bottom? no...), gray gradient (dash), black bottom.

Ugh. The white band might be the gauge ROW (3 gauges side by side, bright) — 3 circles ~0.34 wide each, spanning 1.0 total... the white band looked continuous. 

I'm going in circles with screenshots. Better: take a FULL-SIZE PNG screenshot and inspect closely (the instructions say read full-size PNG when fine detail matters). Let me look at the current PNG with detail.
The spec is re-confirmed — I'm continuing with the cockpit fix. Let me inspect the latest screenshot at full resolution to identify exactly what's blocking the view:

Actually — a cleaner approach to the whole cockpit rendering: build a proper cockpit VIEW that doesn't depend on hiding exterior meshes: 
- In cockpit mode, RENDER ONLY: world (scene minus aircraft) + cockpit group. I.e., hide the entire aircraft group EXCEPT the cockpit subgroup. GAME.cockpit.group is a CHILD of ac.group. Setting ac.group.visible=false hides children incl. cockpit. Instead, I can RE-PARENT the cockpit group to the scene at spawn, and each frame copy the aircraft's world transform to it (it's a static 1:1 child transform: position/quaternion/scale = ac.group).
```js
// no — simpler: reparent to scene, and in the render loop:
cockpit.group.position.copy(ac.group.position);
cockpit.group.quaternion.copy(ac.group.quaternion);
```

- Finish the existing playable mobile-first 3D flight simulator and resolve the remaining cockpit-view issue.

## Requirements
- Deliver a complete, integrated, playable flight simulator with aircraft, force-based flight, functional systems and controls, procedural environment, weather, audio, mobile UI, and graphics presets.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save visual-check screenshots as small JPEGs at viewport width ≤1280px; read only the latest screenshot.

- Implemented as a browser-based Three.js game rather than Unity/Unreal, using procedural aircraft and world assets.
- Uses a custom 6DOF force-based flight model and a debug API exposed as `window.SIM`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game systems across `index.html` and `src/`; aircraft, physics, environment, controls, audio, and HUD are integrated.
- Fixed prior flight-model issues; verified takeoff and climb for the Cessna, jet, and airliner, plus stall/recovery, Cessna and jet landings, braking/reverse/spoilers, and crash/restart.
- Verified external and chase views; saved screenshots under `screenshots/`.
- Fixed spawn touchdown toast and made cockpit visibility/lights and enclosing aircraft visibility respond to cockpit mode.
- Reparented the cockpit group to the scene and aligned it to the aircraft when entering cockpit view.

### Active
- Finish and visually verify cockpit view: latest screenshot still has pure-black horizontal bands despite aircraft exterior being hidden and cockpit being scene-level. `#cockpitGlow` CSS is the next suspected source to inspect.

- Cockpit view remains visually unresolved; black bands are confirmed by pixel sampling, but their cause is not yet established.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: game setup, cameras, cockpit visibility, update loop, and `SIM` debug API.

## Objective
- Finish the existing playable mobile-first 3D flight simulator, including diagnosing and fixing the cockpit-view black bands and verifying the visuals.

## Requirements
- Deliver an integrated, playable flight simulator with aircraft, force-based flight, functional systems and controls, procedural environment, weather, audio, mobile UI, and graphics presets.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save visual-check screenshots as small JPEGs at viewport width ≤1280px; read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a browser-based Three.js game with procedural aircraft and world assets.
- Uses a custom 6DOF force-based flight model and exposes a debug API as `window.SIM`.
- Reduced the cockpit vignette and made instrument faces double-sided to address likely sources of dark cockpit bands and invisible gauges.

## Work State
### Completed
- Integrated aircraft, physics, environment, controls, audio, HUD, and related game systems across `index.html` and `src/`.
- Prior scripted checks verified takeoff and climb for the Cessna, jet, and airliner; stall/recovery, Cessna and jet landings, braking/reverse/spoilers, and crash/restart.
- Fixed spawn touchdown toast and made cockpit visibility/lights and exterior aircraft visibility respond to cockpit mode.
- Reparented the cockpit group to the scene and aligned it to the aircraft when entering cockpit view.
- Changed cockpit vignette styling in `index.html` and set gauge planes to `THREE.DoubleSide` in `src/aircraft.js`.
- Ran Chromium checks at 1200×675 for external, cockpit, night, and storm modes; `SIM` showed expected camera visibility/mode values and no page errors.
- Saved `screenshots/latest-cockpit.jpg`.

### Active
- Read and visually inspect `screenshots/latest-cockpit.jpg` to confirm cockpit bands and panel/gauges are resolved.
- Review external, night, and storm visuals; screenshots currently only saved for cockpit.
- Review final diff and summarize changes and assumptions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Read the latest `screenshots/latest-cockpit.jpg` and confirm cockpit panel visibility and absence of black bands.
2. If needed, capture and inspect external/night/storm screenshots at ≤1280px.
3. Review `git diff` and repository status; report verification and any remaining caveats.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI/CSS and cockpit vignette `#cockpitGlow`.
- `src/main.js`: camera modes, cockpit visibility, update loop, and `SIM` debug API.
- `src/aircraft.js`: aircraft definitions, cockpit geometry, and instrument faces.
- `src/physics.js`: flight model, ground contact, engine/systems, and crash logic.
- `src/world.js`: procedural terrain, airport, city, and population.
- `src/env.js`: lighting, weather, wind, and turbulence.
- `screenshots/latest-cockpit.jpg`: latest cockpit visual-check image.

## Important Context
- Repository changes are uncommitted.
- Cockpit camera uses `spec.cam.cockpit` and flips the aircraft quaternion by π around Y; cockpit geometry is positioned from the same cockpit coordinates.
- In cockpit mode the aircraft exterior is hidden, the scene-level cockpit is aligned to the aircraft, and `#cockpitGlow` is displayed.
- Prior screenshot `screenshots/12-cockpit.jpg` was unavailable; the fresh screenshot is `screenshots/latest-cockpit.jpg`.
- Local test server was started with `python3 -m http.server 8000`; its shell process may still be running.
